This explains the repeated values I noted earlier. The output grid values represent the unique elements of the original matrix, which are expanded in the input according to some patterns.

I see that the row and column sequences indicate how many times the rows and columns of the base matrix are repeated in the input. Further, within that subgrid, identical rows indicate identical f values, establishing a mapping between identical rows and indices. This is important!

Since examples have distinct rows, I'm focusing on preserving the order to define the mapping. I'm focusing on cropping the non-zero bounding box. Now, I will keep only unique rows in order.

I'm now putting the final pieces together, reconstructing the original matrix. I'm focusing on preserving the order of rows and columns as I filter for uniqueness. Specifically, I'm verifying the process of taking unique rows of the subgrid in order, then unique columns in order of appearance. The resulting matrix, formed by combining those unique rows and columns, matches the output. I've confirmed this with Example 1 and Example 2!
